text: Cascade Outdoor Supply, ticket forty-seven-ninety-eight. A GL accountant is trying to upload a journal spreadsheet and getting a workbook integrity error they've never seen before. It worked fine last week.

Quick distinction from last lesson: FBDI stages bulk data through an interface table, built for volume. ADFdi is different — an Excel add-in connecting a spreadsheet directly to a Fusion page, letting someone enter data in familiar rows and upload it directly, no staging table. It's built for smaller, interactive entry, like Create Journals in Spreadsheet, not massive bulk loads.

The error itself — an integration integrity check failing — points at the add-in or the workbook, not the data. Asking what changed since last week: IT pushed a scheduled environment patch over the weekend. Checking the accountant's installed ADFdi add-in version against what the environment now expects: they're out of sync. The server side updated. The desktop client didn't.

So the client is correctly refusing to upload with a mismatched integration rather than risk something going wrong silently. The fix: update the desktop ADFdi add-in to match the current environment version, and download a fresh copy of the spreadsheet template rather than reusing last week's file, since an old workbook can carry integration metadata tied to the previous version. Worth knowing separately: ADFdi also runs its own validation rules at the worksheet level, catching bad data like an invalid account before it ever reaches the server — if this had been a specific field rejection instead of an integrity error, the fix would be correcting the data, not reinstalling anything.

Resolution note: name the version mismatch specifically, confirm the fix with a successful upload, and recommend IT flag ADFdi version checks in patch notifications going forward. Up next, lesson twenty-eight: when an integration isn't a spreadsheet at all, but a REST API call.
